message.content:
The total number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—on the order of **10⁴³**. This estimate (often called the “Shannon number” for positions) comes from counting all ways the 32 pieces can be arranged on the 64 squares while respecting the rules of chess (e.g., no two kings in check, pawn promotion possibilities, etc.). 

For comparison, the number of possible complete games (sequences of moves from start to finish) is even larger, roughly **10¹²³**. Both figures illustrate why exhaustive search of the entire game tree is infeasible.
